step1_analysis.description: A cross-coupled NMOS LC VCO core with NMOS inversion-mode varactors and a PMOS tail current source. It generates the high-frequency clock for the fractional-N frequency synthesizer.

paper_reference.title: A 2.4-GHz Monolithic Fractional-N Frequency Synthesizer With Robust Phase-Switching Prescaler and Loop Capacitance Multiplier

center_frequency.description: Center oscillation frequency of the VCO

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the LC tank. With L=20nH and C=0.15pF per side (added in testbench), plus varactor capacitance (~20fF), f = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(20nH*0.17pF)) ≈ 2.7 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Tank components in the testbench are sized to target the 2.4 GHz ISM band while accommodating the small default varactor sizes.

tuning_range.description: Percentage frequency variation across the control voltage range

sky130_expected.calculation: Varactor capacitance changes from ~21fF (inversion) to ~10fF (depletion). With a 150fF fixed tank capacitor, total C changes by ~7%, leading to a ~3.5% frequency shift.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The tuning range is limited by the small default W/L (5u/0.5u) of the varactors in the provided netlist compared to the fixed tank capacitance needed for 2.4 GHz.

power_consumption.description: DC power dissipated by the VCO core

sky130_expected.calculation: I_tail is set by the PMOS mirror (W=5u, L=0.5u). V_ov ≈ 0.39V -> I_tail ≈ 38 uA. Power = 38 uA * 1.8 V = 68 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The expected power is much lower than the paper because the extracted netlist uses minimum/small default transistor sizes (5um) rather than the large devices typically used in a low-phase-noise VCO.

oscillation_amplitude.description: Peak-to-peak voltage swing of the oscillator outputs

sky130_expected.calculation: V_swing = I_tail * R_p. With I_tail = 38 uA and an ideal tank R_p = 20 kOhm, V_swing = 0.76 V peak (1.52 V peak-to-peak differential).
sky130_expected.reasoning: A high-Q ideal tank is used in the testbench to ensure startup with the small default transconductance (gm) of the cross-coupled pair.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure oscillation frequency, tuning range, amplitude, and power consumption at minimum and maximum control voltages.
step3_testbench.spice:
* LC VCO Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VIBIAS IBIAS 0 0.99
VVC VC 0 0.0

* DUT
XM1 VO_PLUS VO_MINUS GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 VO_MINUS VO_PLUS GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N1 IBIAS VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 VC VO_PLUS VC VC sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 IBIAS IBIAS VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 VC VO_MINUS VC VC sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}

* Ideal LC Tank components (added to enable oscillation with default small W/L)
L1 VO_PLUS N1 20n
R1 VO_PLUS N1 20k
L2 VO_MINUS N1 20n
R2 VO_MINUS N1 20k
C1 VO_PLUS GND 0.15p
C2 VO_MINUS GND 0.15p

* Initial condition to kickstart oscillation
.ic v(vo_plus)=1.8 v(vo_minus)=0.0

.control
  * Run 1: VC = 0V (Max varactor capacitance, Min frequency)
  alter VVC 0
  tran 2p 40n
  
  * Measure frequency over 10 cycles in steady state
  meas tran t_start1 trig v(vo_plus) val=0.6 rise=40
  meas tran t_end1 trig v(vo_plus) val=0.6 rise=50
  let freq_min = 10 / (t_end1 - t_start1)
  
  * Measure amplitude and power
  meas tran v_max max v(vo_plus) from=20n to=40n
  meas tran v_min min v(vo_plus) from=20n to=40n
  let v_amp = v_max - v_min
  
  meas tran i_vdd avg i(VVDD) from=20n to=40n
  let power = -i_vdd * 1.8
  
  * Run 2: VC = 1.8V (Min varactor capacitance, Max frequency)
  alter VVC 1.8
  tran 2p 40n
  
  meas tran t_start2 trig v(vo_plus) val=0.6 rise=40
  meas tran t_end2 trig v(vo_plus) val=0.6 rise=50
  let freq_max = 10 / (t_end2 - t_start2)
  
  * Calculate tuning metrics
  let tuning_range = freq_max - freq_min
  let center_freq = (freq_max + freq_min) / 2
  let tuning_percent = (tuning_range / center_freq) * 100
  
  print freq_min freq_max center_freq tuning_range tuning_percent
  print v_amp power
  
  quit
.endc
